editor.title: Benedictus Richard Ricardo
editor.lede: I work where processes cross teams, handoffs lose clarity, or important work depends on one person’s memory. I make those workflows clear, documented, and repeatable.
body: A good system makes the next step clear, reduces avoidable repetition, and helps teams work reliably under pressure.
I am studying Data Science at Universitas Terbuka, where I am strengthening my approach to process design through data and evidence.

contact.title: Let’s make the work run better.
contact.body: If your team spends too much time on manual work, unclear handoffs, or live-event coordination, let’s talk. I am based in GMT+7 and work across systems, automation, and operations.

automation-mandate.metaDescription: How a shared reporting system cut more than 12 hours of manual work each week at Home Digital Indonesia.
automation-mandate.title: A reporting system that saves the team 12+ hours each week.
automation-mandate.deck: I redesigned the reporting workflow and its supporting procedures, removing more than 12 hours of manual work each week. The team can now repeat the process reliably without depending on one person.
automation-mandate.imageAlt: A conceptual process map joining three workstreams into a shared reporting system.
automation-mandate.caption: An original visual interpretation of the reporting workflow described in this case study.
automation-mandate.lead: Three functions were spending too much time each week on the same manual reporting cycle. The key improvement was a clear, shared process rather than additional software.

process.title: From manual handoffs to one weekly rhythm
process.description: Three functions. One reporting structure. A routine the team could repeat.

narrative.heading: Context
narrative.body: Finance, sales, and operations were collecting the same information, reformatting spreadsheets, and handing off incomplete files. The process worked, but it required significant time and depended too heavily on individual memory.

narrative.heading: What was built
narrative.body: I redesigned the Excel workbook logic and documented shared procedures for each step. I also mapped the reporting workflow end to end so the team could follow the same process each Monday with fewer errors and handoff delays.

narrative.heading: Outcome
narrative.body: The redesigned workflow removed about 12 hours of manual work each week. It also clarified responsibilities and allowed the team to maintain the process when someone was away.

automation-mandate.pull: More than 12 hours of manual work removed each week, replaced by a process the team can repeat.
evidence: Built Excel reporting automation that saves the team more than 12 hours of manual work each week.
Documented shared procedures for finance, sales, and operations to make the reporting cycle consistent.
Replaced person-dependent reminders with a documented weekly standard.

impact.label: Hours saved each week
impact.note: Manual reporting effort removed from the recurring cycle.

impact.label: Functions aligned
impact.note: Finance, sales, and operations on one structure.

impact.label: Shared routine
impact.note: Automation and SOPs combined into a repeatable weekly flow.

kpi-governance-record.metaDescription: How a 34-member student council used clear KPIs and regular reviews to coordinate 10 divisions.
kpi-governance-record.title: A 34-member student council established clear accountability.
kpi-governance-record.deck: How a student council introduced KPIs and regular reviews to coordinate its programs and responsibilities more consistently.
kpi-governance-record.bylineRole: Student Council President · SMA Santa Maria 2
kpi-governance-record.imageAlt: A 34-person council represented as ten connected divisions around a shared operating rhythm.
kpi-governance-record.caption: A conceptual visual of the governance rhythm described in this case study.
kpi-governance-record.lead: A 34-member student council across ten divisions needed clearer responsibilities and better visibility into program delivery. KPIs and weekly reviews created a shared operating rhythm.

process.title: Make progress visible across ten divisions
process.description: Clear expectations and weekly reviews gave the council a shared view of progress.
process.beforeLabel: Before · updates without a shared view

narrative.heading: Context
narrative.body: As a student organization grows across multiple divisions, informal communication alone is not enough. The council needed clearer visibility, consistent follow-through, and a way to review programs while they were underway.

narrative.heading: What was built
narrative.body: I introduced measurable expectations, regular progress reviews, and clearer links between each division’s work and the council’s goals. Weekly KPI reviews gave the team a consistent basis for planning and follow-through.

narrative.heading: Outcome
narrative.body: The council gained a clearer view of progress, blockers, and where support was needed. Programs became more consistent, and outreach activities reached twelve partner schools.

kpi-governance-record.pull: Teams are easier to lead when everyone can see the work and its progress.
evidence: Led a 34-member council across ten divisions using KPIs and weekly progress reviews.
Designed school-wide programs that the administration adopted as ongoing initiatives.
Coordinated outreach activities that reached twelve partner schools.

impact.label: Members led
impact.note: Leadership scope across the full organization.

impact.label: Partner schools reached
impact.note: Scale of one major outward-facing campaign.

large-scale-event-ops.title: Reliable operations for events with 1,000+ attendees.
large-scale-event-ops.deck: Three years coordinating stage and backstage operations for large events, including hosting a youth service attended by more than 500 people.
large-scale-event-ops.bylineRole: Stage Coordinator & MC · Ultimate Event Organizer
large-scale-event-ops.imageAlt: A stage plan with light beams and cue lines representing live transitions.
large-scale-event-ops.caption: A visual interpretation of cueing, pacing and backstage handoffs.
large-scale-event-ops.lead: Large events depend on precise transitions, clear coordination, and well-managed backstage operations. Small breakdowns are immediately visible, so every team needs a shared plan.

process.title: Give every transition a clear next move
process.description: A shared running order helps crews, speakers, and performers move through a live program with clear handoffs.
before: Cues for crew, speakers, and performers

narrative.heading: Context
narrative.body: When a stage transition is unclear, the audience notices immediately. The challenge at a large public event is to keep timing, technical cues, and handoffs reliable under pressure.

narrative.heading: What was built
narrative.body: I translated the running order into clear steps for the technical crew, speakers, and performers. This included planning transitions in advance and coordinating teams throughout the event.

narrative.heading: Outcome
narrative.body: The work improved transition clarity and helped the stage team maintain the schedule under pressure. At the 2025 youth service, I hosted more than 500 attendees while coordinating the live program.

large-scale-event-ops.pull: Consistent timing makes a live event feel considered. Unclear transitions are immediately visible.
evidence: Coordinated backstage operations for events attended by more than 1,000 people.
Hosted the 2025 youth service for more than 500 attendees and coordinated the program flow.
Reduced transition friction with a clearer running order and team handoffs.

impact.label: Audience scale
impact.note: Large live-event environments with visible execution pressure.

impact.label: Attendees hosted
impact.note: Youth Mass 2025 as a proof point for live communication.

vertical-rescue-ops.metaDescription: A look at equipment readiness, technical training, and field operations at Vertical Rescue Indonesia.
vertical-rescue-ops.title: Readiness is built long before a field assignment.
vertical-rescue-ops.deck: More than four years supporting equipment care and technical training at Vertical Rescue Indonesia. Readiness depends on consistent checks and disciplined preparation.
vertical-rescue-ops.imageAlt: Inspection marks and technical equipment shapes representing training readiness.
vertical-rescue-ops.caption: A conceptual illustration of equipment checks and training preparation.
vertical-rescue-ops.lead: Readiness work happens out of view, but it determines whether equipment, people, and procedures are dependable when conditions become difficult.

process.title: Build confidence before field training
process.description: Equipment care and training support establish dependable practices before technical exercises begin.

narrative.heading: Context
narrative.body: Technical rescue depends on disciplined preparation. Equipment checks, regular practice, and clear roles need to be in place before conditions become challenging.

narrative.heading: What was built
narrative.body: I maintain and inspect equipment, support technical climbing sessions as a lead climber and belayer, and help new trainees develop safe, repeatable practices.

narrative.heading: Outcome
narrative.body: Consistent equipment checks and training support strengthen operational readiness and give new trainees a more reliable foundation before field exercises.

vertical-rescue-ops.pull: In technical work, confidence comes from preparation and consistency.
evidence: Maintained equipment readiness through regular inspections and routine care.
Supported technical climbing and belay exercises as part of the training team.
Reinforced a safety culture in which preparation is part of the standard.

impact.label: Years active
impact.note: Sustained involvement in readiness and training work.

impact.label: Equipment checks
impact.note: Inspection and maintenance as part of the standard.

impact.label: Training support
impact.note: Hands-on support for climbing and belay training.
